children: Fears of a looming U.S. sovereign debt crisis are fundamentally misplaced due to nearly $500T in private sector assets that currently dwarf the nation's public liabilities, according to Discipline Funds Founder and Chief Investment Officer Cullen Roche.
market, Roche characterized the panic as mostly "recency bias". He noted in a social media post Thursday that the 10-year yield
has averaged 5.8% since 1960, meaning the current 5.19% level is actually below the long-term historical average.
"Ignore all the sovereign debt crisis talk," Roche wrote, adding that "inflation expectations are adjusting to something more historically normalized."

Roche argued that those who focus heavily on the debt crisis narrative commit a "fallacy of composition" by looking exclusively at public liabilities while ignoring massive growth on the asset side of the ledger. He describes the aggregate U.S. economy's balance sheet as the healthiest in the world, noting that interest rates have remained largely stable over the last 20 years specifically because the private sector—the tax base for the U.S. government—remains incredibly strong.

To illustrate this economic foundation, the macro strategist pointed to data showing that total gross private sector assets sit around $489T. Because these private sector assets are roughly ten times larger than the public debt they ultimately fund, any conversation about national liabilities must be contextualized by this nearly half-quadrillion-dollar asset base, Roche insisted.

title: The $489T reason to stop worrying about U.S. debt
